Done. Branch `feat/file-upload-retries` with 4 commits on top of `40ffab1`.

## Root cause

Retries only work when the request body can be re-sent: `retryTransport` requires a replayable body (`pipedrive/retry.go:86` — `nil`/`NoBody`/`GetBody != nil`), and `RetryAllMethods` doesn't bypass that (it only gates 502/503/504; 429 always needs replayability). `http.NewRequest` sets `GetBody` only for `*bytes.Buffer`/`*bytes.Reader`/`*strings.Reader`. A multipart body streamed from `os.Open` has none of those → every 429 surfaced immediately as `RateLimitError`. Call-log recording uploads work because `multipartbody.NewFile` buffers the file into a `*bytes.Reader` — that's why "every other call retries fine".

## Summary

- **`v1.FilesService.AddFile(ctx, fileName, content, opts…)`** — the ergonomic upload: file name + `io.Reader`, multipart built internally (`file` field), association via `WithFileDealID`/`WithFilePersonID`/`WithFileOrgID`/`WithFileProductID`/`WithFileActivityID`/`WithFileLeadID`/`WithFileProjectID`. Content is buffered so the body is replayable and 429/5xx retries work out of the box.
- **`pipedrive.WithBodyReplacer`** — new request option that makes one-shot bodies (streamed uploads, `Raw.Do`, any v1/v2 service) replayable: the replacer is invoked for the first send and before every retry, so a streaming upload can re-open its file. Fixes the existing `Files.Add` path without changing its signature.
- **`multipartbody.NewFileWithFields`** — internal helper writes text fields alongside the file part (`NewFile` now delegates).
- Docs: CHANGELOG entry + README note in the retries section.

Migration: `client.Files.Add(ctx, myMultipartBody, contentType)` → `client.Files.AddFile(ctx, name, f, WithFileDealID(...))`; keep `Add` for custom bodies and add `pipedrive.WithBodyReplacer(func() (io.Reader, error) { f, _ := os.Open(path); … })` if you must stream.
